text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Multiple NotReady nodes detected in cluster 'infer-usw-1' affecting inference-pools (auto-pager). 12:02 UTC.

emma (oncall): seeing the alert. checking grafana now.

emma (oncall): pods on node infer-usw-1a are failing Liveness with 'context deadline exceeded' and kubelet reconnects.

dinesh: can you paste the node status? I just pulled `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep infer-usw-1` — a bunch show NotReady.

carla: runtime reports from the node show repeated kubelet restarts, and `nvidia-smi` responses are intermittent. suspect driver/kernel hitch + kubelet flapping.

emma (oncall): customer impact: routing shows 11% 5xx from us-west region over the last 3m, 95p latency from 210ms -> 1.2s for small-gen workloads. Loadbalancer bumped to retry mode.

riley: pulling kubelet logs now. `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager` shows a cycle: "E kubelet: container runtime socket closed" then restart. also messages about oom_score_adj for a shim.

carla: runtime agent logs from inference container: repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` followed by container kill by OOM killer. likely memory leak in a particular model variant (hf/ggml-xx) under long sequences.

emma (oncall): OK mitigation plan: 1) cordon the most flappy nodes 2) drain pods from them (evict inference pods) 3) route traffic away from infer-usw-1 pool to infer-usw-2 and fallback model variants 4) scale up Dedicated fallback pool if needed. executing steps now.

marta: i'm cordoning infer-usw-1a and infer-usw-1b: `kubectl cordon infer-usw-1a && kubectl cordon infer-usw-1b` :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Node cordoned: infer-usw-1a by marta.

emma (oncall): draining with `kubectl drain infer-usw-1a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` -- watch for long-lived stateful pods.

carla: while draining, I'm updating runtime routing policies to avoid prefers=usw-1 for inference-pool tag. applying policy change in control plane now.

incident-bot: [ACTION] Canary routing rule updated: prefer infer-usw-2 over infer-usw-1 for tag:inference-pool.

riley: scaling up infer-usw-2 autoscaler +1 replica set for quick capacity: `kubectl scale deployment/infer-runtime -n inference --replicas=6`

marta: drains completed, but a few pods failed to reschedule due to nodeSelector for gpu-type=v100. spotted ~4 pods in Pending because capacity mismatch.

carla: rolling fallback: enabling quantized model variant for routing (q8 instead of fp16) to reduce memory. updating model-router config: `model-router set-weight ggml-xx-q8=0.6, ggml-xx-fp16=0.4`

emma (oncall): customers impacted: two larger customers had 5xx spikes, notified CS. created incident ticket INC-2026-224 with customer IDs.

dinesh: investigating hardware: `dmesg` on the flappy node shows repeated GPU reset: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79, PID 1234" and kernel messages about "GPU hung, resetting". Might be driver/kernel mismatch introduced in recent node image update.

riley: rolling restart of kubelet on healthy node for comparison: `systemctl restart kubelet` — no immediate issues on node infer-usw-2.

carla: collecting heapdumps and nvml logs from suspect containers: uploading to /tmp/inc-3860123456 on S3. Grab the core dump before purge.

marta: three pods still failing recreate on infer-usw-2 due to nodeAffinity strict rules. I've created a temporary taint on infer-usw-1 to prevent schedule and added toleration on infer-usw-2 test nodes.

incident-bot: [METRIC] us-west: 5xx rate = 11.8% (5m), request rate down 8%.

emma (oncall): status update for incident channel: short summary + mitigation actions, tagging @support to prep customer comms.

carla: root cause hypothesis: sudden driver resets causing CUDA failures -> container OOMs -> kubelet sees repeated container crashes -> kubelet restarts (or panics) -> node NotReady. Need to revert driver update rolled last night in image if confirmed.

dinesh: checking image builds: edge image 2026.03.10 pushed to sortie last night with nvidia-driver 535.11. a rollback to 535.4 was stable historically. engineering change initiated?

riley: suggestion: scale up fallback pool in another AZ and failover traffic; also add a temporary autoscale policy to accept pending GPU-specific pods.

marta: capacity charity: launched 2 extra nodes in infer-usw-2 with driver 535.4 via terraform: `tfe run apply -var 'node_image=2026.03.05'` — nodes booting.

ops-bot: AMI bake job finished (id: bake-3860123456) using image 2026.03.05.

emma (oncall): ok, primary mitigation in place: cordoned bad nodes, drained, routing updated, fallback nodes coming up, quantized models routing. Customer impact reduced but still elevated. Next steps: continue collecting logs, confirm driver rollback plan, and schedule full node replacement for nodes with repeated GPU resets.

carla: I recommend marking the affected nodes for reprovisioning rather than in-place driver fiddling. Hardware vendor might need to inspect. I'll attach collected NVML logs to the ticket.

dinesh: I'll open an infra change to redeploy those hosts with the stable image and track with change-id CHG-386012.

riley: monitoring: 5xx dropped to 3.1% after routing changes and extra capacity. 95p latency back to 310ms. continuing watch for 15m.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] Severity: S2 -> investigating. Page suppressed.

emma (oncall): folks, I'm going to handoff to @riley for overnight watch. Riley — can you take the pager and own follow-ups (driver rollback, nodes reprovision, customer updates)?

riley: taking handoff. I'll keep the incident channel open and post updates. cadence: 15m.

emma (oncall): leaving a note in the incident ticket: mitigations performed, nodes cordoned, fallback scaled, probable driver-induced GPU resets. link: https://redwood.ops/incident/3860123456

marta: final checklist before handoff: collect `kubectl describe node` for flappy nodes, nvml logs, kubelet journals, docker/containerd logs, and upload to incident S3. done.

ops-bot: Upload complete: s3://redwood-incidents/3860123456/logs.tar.gz

riley: acknowledged. will coordinate the image rollback change with dinesh and update the incident. tagging infra lead @carla for reprovision decision.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE?] No — monitoring watch continues.

emma (oncall): leaving the channel. good work everyone. :heart:

riley: thanks — will ping if anything regresses.
